title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 11. The Glory of Mahaprasada
html:
The Lord comes to the house of Sarvabhauma, who, astonished by His form, sends his younger brother with Him to the temple; at the sight of Jagannatha the Lord falls senseless, recovers in Sarvabhauma's house and partakes of mahaprasada, whose glory the poet proclaims

Verse 1

तच्छ्रुत्वा प्राह विप्रेन्द्रः श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः।
कथं दृष्टो भगवता पुरुषोत्तम ईश्वरः॥१॥

tacchrutvā prāha viprendraḥ śrīdāmodarapaṇḍitaḥ|
kathaṁ dṛṣṭo bhagavatā puruṣottama īśvaraḥ||1||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; praha — said; vipra-indrah — the best of brahmanas; shri-damodara-panditah — Sri Damodara Pandita; katham — how; drishtah — was seen; bhagavata — by Bhagavan; purushottamah — Purushottama; ishvarah — the Lord.

1Having heard this, Sri Damodara Pandita, the best of brahmanas, asked, "How did Bhagavan see the Lord Purushottama?

Verse 2

दृष्टः केन किमकरोत्स्वयमेव जनार्दनः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा प्राह स गुप्तस्तुष्टो वैद्यः कथां शुभाम्॥२॥

dṛṣṭaḥ kena kimakarotsvayameva janārdanaḥ|
tacchrutvā prāha sa guptastuṣṭo vaidyaḥ kathāṁ śubhām||2||

drishtah — seen; kena — by whom (with whose help); kim — what; akarot — did; svayam — Himself; eva — indeed; janardanah — Janardana; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; praha — told; sah — he; guptah — Gupta; tushtah — pleased; vaidyah — the physician; katham — the account; shubham — auspicious.

2Who helped Him to see Him, and what did Janardana Himself do?" Hearing this, Gupta the physician was pleased and began the auspicious account.

Verse 3

शृणुष्वावहितं ब्रह्मन्दिव्यां त्रैलोक्यपावनीम्।
कथां श्रीजगदीशस्य दर्शनानन्दसम्भवाम्॥३॥

śṛṇuṣvāvahitaṁ brahmandivyāṁ trailokyapāvanīm|
kathāṁ śrījagadīśasya darśanānandasambhavām||3||

shrinushva — hear; avahitam — attentively; brahman — O brahmana; divyam — divine; trailokya-pavanim — purifying the three worlds; katham — account; shri-jagadishasya — of Sri Jagadisha, the Lord of the world; darshana-ananda-sambhavam — born of the bliss of beholding.

3"Listen attentively, O brahmana, to the divine story of Sri Jagadisha, the Lord of the world — a story that purifies the three worlds and is born of the bliss of beholding Him.

Verse 4

गत्वादौ वासुदेवस्य सार्वभौमस्य वेश्मनि।
सत्वरं स समुत्थाय ननाम दण्डवत्सुधीः॥४॥

gatvādau vāsudevasya sārvabhaumasya veśmani|
satvaraṁ sa samutthāya nanāma daṇḍavatsudhīḥ||4||

gatva — having gone; adau — first; vasudevasya — of Vasudeva; sarvabhaumasya — Sarvabhauma; veshmani — to the house; satvaram — hastily; sah — he; samutthaya — rising; nanama — bowed down; danda-vat — like a staff; sudhih — the wise one.

4First the Lord went to the house of Vasudeva Sarvabhauma, and the wise Sarvabhauma rose in haste and bowed down before Him like a staff.

Verse 5

दृष्ट्वा तं प्राह भगवान्सगद्गदगिरा हरिः।
कथं द्रक्ष्यामि देवेशं जगन्नाथं सनातनम्॥५॥

dṛṣṭvā taṁ prāha bhagavānsagadgadagirā hariḥ|
kathaṁ drakṣyāmi deveśaṁ jagannāthaṁ sanātanam||5||

drishtva — seeing; tam — him; praha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sa-gadgada-gira — in a faltering voice; harih — Hari; katham — how; drakshyami — shall I see; deva-isham — the Lord of the gods; jagannatham — Jagannatha; sanatanam — the eternal.

5Seeing him, Hari Bhagavan said in a faltering voice, 'How shall I see Jagannatha, the eternal Lord of the gods?'

Verse 6

इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य सार्वभौमो महायशाः।
प्रकाशिनयनाब्जेन तद्वपुः समलोकयत्॥६॥

iti śrutvā vacastasya sārvabhaumo mahāyaśāḥ|
prakāśinayanābjena tadvapuḥ samalokayat||6||

iti — thus; shrutva — hearing; vachah — the words; tasya — His; sarvabhaumah — Sarvabhauma; maha-yashah — the renowned; prakashi-nayana-abjena — with lotus eyes opened wide; tat-vapuh — His form; samalokayat — looked over.

6Hearing His words, the renowned Sarvabhauma opened wide his lotus eyes and looked Him over.

Verse 7

सुतप्तकाञ्चनाभासं मेरुशृङ्गमिवापरम्।
राकासुधाकराकारमुखं जलजलोचनम्॥७॥

sutaptakāñcanābhāsaṁ meruśṛṅgamivāparam|
rākāsudhākarākāramukhaṁ jalajalocanam||7||

su-tapta-kanchana-abhasam — gleaming like molten gold; meru-shringam — a peak of Meru; iva — like; aparam — another; raka-sudhakara-akara-mukham — His face like the full moon; jalaja-lochanam — lotus-eyed.

7He gleamed like molten gold, like a second peak of Meru; His face was like the full moon, His eyes like lotuses.

Verse 8

सुनसं कम्बुकण्ठाढ्यं महोरस्कं महाभुजम्।
बन्धूकमुकुरारक्तदन्तच्छदमनोहरम्॥८॥

sunasaṁ kambukaṇṭhāḍhyaṁ mahoraskaṁ mahābhujam|
bandhūkamukurāraktadantacchadamanoharam||8||

su-nasam — with a fine nose; kambu-kantha-adhyam — graced with a conch-like neck; maha-uraskam — broad-chested; maha-bhujam — mighty-armed; bandhuka-mukura-arakta-dantachchhada-manoharam — charming with lips red as bandhuka buds.

8His nose was fine, His neck like a conch, His chest broad, His arms mighty, and His lips, red as bandhuka buds, charmed the heart.

Verse 9

कुन्दाभदन्तमत्यन्तचन्द्ररश्मिजितस्मितम्।
आजानुलम्बितभुजं विलसत्पादपङ्कजम्॥९॥

kundābhadantamatyantacandraraśmijitasmitam|
ājānulambitabhujaṁ vilasatpādapaṅkajam||9||

kunda-abha-dantam — with teeth like jasmine; atyanta-chandra-rashmi-jita-smitam — whose smile far surpassed the moonbeams; ajanu-lambita-bhujam — with arms reaching to the knees; vilasat-pada-pankajam — with radiant lotus feet.

9His teeth were like jasmine flowers, His smile far outshone the moonbeams, His arms hung down to His knees, and His lotus feet were radiant.

Verse 10

कृष्णप्रेमोज्ज्वलं शश्वत्पुलकाञ्चितविग्रहम्।
कूर्मोन्नतपदद्वन्द्वं दृष्ट्वादौ विस्मितोऽभवत्॥१०॥

kṛṣṇapremojjvalaṁ śaśvatpulakāñcitavigraham|
kūrmonnatapadadvandvaṁ dṛṣṭvādau vismito'bhavat||10||

krishna-prema-ujjvalam — radiant with love for Krishna; shashvat — constantly; pulaka-anchita-vigraham — His body adorned with bristling hair; kurma-unnata-pada-dvandvam — with feet arched like a tortoise's back; drishtva — seeing; adau — at first; vismitah — astonished; abhavat — became.

10He glowed with love for Krishna, the hair of His body stood constantly on end, and His feet were arched like a tortoise's back. Seeing all this, Sarvabhauma was at first astonished, and he thought:

Verse 11

किमसौ पुरुषव्याघ्रो महापुरुषलक्षणः।
अवतीर्ण इवाभाति वैकुण्ठाद्देवरूपधृक्॥११॥

kimasau puruṣavyāghro mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaḥ|
avatīrṇa ivābhāti vaikuṇṭhāddevarūpadhṛk||11||

kim — can it be; asau — this; purusha-vyaghrah — tiger among men; maha-purusha-lakshanah — bearing the marks of a great person; avatirnah — descended; iva — as if; abhati — appears; vaikunthat — from Vaikuntha; deva-rupa-dhrik — wearing a divine form.

11'Can this tiger among men, bearing the marks of a great person, be a god who has taken form and, as it seems, descended from Vaikuntha?

Verse 12

किं वासौ सच्चिदानन्दरूपवान्रसमूर्तिमान्।
किं वासौ सर्वजीवानां हितकृदीश्वरः स्वयम्॥१२॥

kiṁ vāsau saccidānandarūpavānrasamūrtimān|
kiṁ vāsau sarvajīvānāṁ hitakṛdīśvaraḥ svayam||12||

kim va — or else; asau — this; sat-chit-ananda-rupavan — having a form of being, consciousness and bliss; rasa-murtiman — rasa embodied; kim va — or else; asau — this; sarva-jivanam — of all living beings; hita-krit — the benefactor; ishvarah — the Lord; svayam — Himself.

12Or is He the One whose form is being, consciousness and bliss, rasa embodied? Or is He the Lord Himself, the benefactor of all living beings?'

Verse 13

इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा सोऽनुजं प्राह शुद्धधीः।
गच्छ त्वं श्रीयुतेनाद्य चैतन्येन महात्मना॥१३॥

iti sañcintya manasā so'nujaṁ prāha śuddhadhīḥ|
gaccha tvaṁ śrīyutenādya caitanyena mahātmanā||13||

iti — thus; sanchintya — reflecting; manasa — in his mind; sah — he; anujam — to his younger brother; praha — said; shuddha-dhih — pure of mind; gachchha — go; tvam — you; shri-yutena — with the illustrious; adya — today; chaitanyena — Chaitanya; maha-atmana — the great soul.

13Reflecting thus, Sarvabhauma, pure of mind, said to his younger brother, 'Go today with the illustrious Chaitanya, the great soul,

Verse 14

पुरं भगवतः शीघ्रं यथासौ पुरुषोत्तमम्।
पश्यत्यनन्तपुरुषमनायासेन तत्कुरु॥१४॥

puraṁ bhagavataḥ śīghraṁ yathāsau puruṣottamam|
paśyatyanantapuruṣamanāyāsena tatkuru||14||

puram — to the abode; bhagavatah — of Bhagavan; shighram — quickly; yatha — so that; asau — He; purushottamam — Purushottama; pashyati — may see; ananta-purusham — the infinite Person; anayasena — without difficulty; tat — that; kuru — do.

14quickly to the abode of Bhagavan, and see to it that He beholds Purushottama, the infinite Person, without difficulty.'

Verse 15

तच्छ्रुत्वा सार्वभौमस्य वचनामृतमद्भुतम्।
ययौ तस्यानुजो धीमांश्चैतन्येन सहायवान्॥१५॥

tacchrutvā sārvabhaumasya vacanāmṛtamadbhutam|
yayau tasyānujo dhīmāṁścaitanyena sahāyavān||15||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; sarvabhaumasya — of Sarvabhauma; vachana-amritam — the nectar of the words; adbhutam — wonderful; yayau — went; tasya — his; anujah — younger brother; dhiman — the intelligent; chaitanyena — with Chaitanya; sahayavan — as His companion.

15Hearing Sarvabhauma's wonderful, nectarean words, his intelligent younger brother set out together with Chaitanya.

Verse 16

तेन सार्धं स भगवान्गत्वा श्रीहरिमन्दिरम्।
ददर्श पुण्डरीकाक्षं पुरुषोत्तममीश्वरम्॥१६॥

tena sārdhaṁ sa bhagavāngatvā śrīharimandiram|
dadarśa puṇḍarīkākṣaṁ puruṣottamamīśvaram||16||

tena — with him; sardham — together; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; gatva — going; shri-hari-mandiram — to the temple of Sri Hari; dadarsha — beheld; pundarika-aksham — the Lotus-eyed; purushottamam — Purushottama; ishvaram — the Lord.

16Going with him to the temple of Sri Hari, Bhagavan beheld the lotus-eyed Lord Purushottama.

Verse 17

दृष्ट्वोल्लसद्विह्वलिताङ्गयष्टिः
प्रेमाश्रुवारिझरपूरितपीनवक्षाः।
कम्पोद्गतप्रचुरवारियुतेन्दुवक्त्रो
हेमाद्रिशृङ्ग इव वातकृतः पपात॥१७॥

dṛṣṭvollasadvihvalitāṅgayaṣṭiḥ
premāśruvārijharapūritapīnavakṣāḥ|
kampodgatapracuravāriyutenduvaktro
hemādriśṛṅga iva vātakṛtaḥ papāta||17||

drishtva — seeing; ullasat-vihvalita-anga-yashtih — His slender body trembling with rapture; prema-ashru-vari-jhara-purita-pina-vakshah — His broad chest flooded with streams of tears of love; kampa-udgata-prachura-vari-yuta-indu-vaktrah — His moon-face bathed in abundant tears as trembling arose; hema-adri-shringah — a peak of the golden mountain; iva — like; vata-kritah — toppled by the wind; papata — fell.

17No sooner had He seen Him than His slender body trembled with rapture, His broad chest was flooded with streams of tears of love, a shiver ran through Him, His moon-face was bathed in abundant tears — and He fell like a peak of the golden mountain toppled by the wind1.

Verse 18

भूमौ मुमोह भगवान्कृतमुष्टिहस्तो
विस्रस्तवस्त्ररसनो विवशं विदित्वा।
तं ते द्विजाः सपदि बाहुयुगेन धृत्वा
कृत्वाग्रतो भगवतः परतो निनिन्युः॥१८॥

bhūmau mumoha bhagavānkṛtamuṣṭihasto
visrastavastrarasano vivaśaṁ viditvā|
taṁ te dvijāḥ sapadi bāhuyugena dhṛtvā
kṛtvāgrato bhagavataḥ parato nininyuḥ||18||

bhumau — on the ground; mumoha — swooned; bhagavan — Bhagavan; krita-mushti-hastah — His hands clenched into fists; visrasta-vastra-rasanah — His cloth and belt slipping off; vivasham — helpless; viditva — perceiving; tam — Him; te — those; dvijah — brahmanas; sapadi — at once; bahu-yugena — with both arms; dhritva — holding; kritva — placing; agratah — in front (of themselves); bhagavatah — from Bhagavan (Jagannatha); paratah — away; ninyuh — led.

18Bhagavan lay senseless on the ground, His hands clenched into fists, His cloth and belt slipping off. Seeing Him helpless, the brahmanas at once caught Him up in their arms and bore Him before them away from Bhagavan2.

Verse 19

श्रीसार्वभौमवरवेश्मनि लब्धसंज्ञः
सङ्कीर्तनं नरहरेः पुनरेव चक्रे।
नृत्यं च तत्र पुलकावलिपूरिताङ्गो
गाङ्गेयगौरवपुषा पुरुषाधिराजः॥१९॥

śrīsārvabhaumavaraveśmani labdhasaṁjñaḥ
saṅkīrtanaṁ narahareḥ punareva cakre|
nṛtyaṁ ca tatra pulakāvalipūritāṅgo
gāṅgeyagauravapuṣā puruṣādhirājaḥ||19||

shri-sarvabhauma-vara-veshmani — in the fine house of Sri Sarvabhauma; labdha-samjnah — regaining consciousness; sankirtanam — sankirtana; nara-hareh — of Narahari; punah — again; eva — indeed; chakre — performed; nrityam — dance; cha — and; tatra — there; pulaka-avali-purita-angah — His limbs covered with rows of bristling hair; gangeya-gaura-vapusha — with a body golden as gold; purusha-adhirajah — the sovereign of all persons.

19Regaining consciousness in the fine house of Sri Sarvabhauma, He again began the sankirtana of Narahari3 and danced there — the sovereign of all persons, His golden body covered with rows of bristling hair.

Verse 20

भिक्षां चकार भगवान्स निजेन सार्धं
भक्तेन दत्तममृतं सुमहाप्रसादम्।
अन्नं रसायनवरं भवरोगिणां यद्
देवेन्द्रदुर्लभतरं पुरुषोत्तमस्य॥२०॥

bhikṣāṁ cakāra bhagavānsa nijena sārdhaṁ
bhaktena dattamamṛtaṁ sumahāprasādam|
annaṁ rasāyanavaraṁ bhavarogiṇāṁ yad
devendradurlabhataraṁ puruṣottamasya||20||

bhiksham — the meal (alms); chakara — took; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sah — He; nijena — with His own; sardham — together; bhaktena — by the devotee; dattam — given; amritam — the nectar; su-maha-prasadam — the great mahaprasada; annam — food; rasayana-varam — the best elixir; bhava-roginam — for those sick with worldly existence; yat — which; deva-indra-durlabha-taram — hardest to obtain even for Indra; purushottamasya — of Purushottama.

20Then Bhagavan, together with His devotee, took His meal: the nectar of Purushottama's great mahaprasada, offered by that devotee — food that is the best of elixirs for those sick with the disease of worldly existence, and beyond the reach even of Indra.

Verse 21

भुक्त्वा यदन्नमखिलं वृजिनं जहाति
धर्मार्थकाममममृतं च तथा महत्त्वम्।
प्राप्नोति बालिशजनो यदि नैव भुङ्क्ते
गच्छेत शूकरगतिं स च धर्महीनः॥२१॥

bhuktvā yadannamakhilaṁ vṛjinaṁ jahāti
dharmārthakāmamamamṛtaṁ ca tathā mahattvam|
prāpnoti bāliśajano yadi naiva bhuṅkte
gaccheta śūkaragatiṁ sa ca dharmahīnaḥ||21||

bhuktva — having eaten; yat — which; annam — food; akhilam — all; vrijinam — sin; jahati — one casts off; dharma-artha-kamam — dharma, wealth and desire; amritam — immortality; cha — and; tatha — also; mahattvam — greatness; prapnoti — one obtains; balisha-janah — a foolish person; yadi — if; na — not; eva — at all; bhunkte — eats; gachchheta — would go; shukara-gatim — the way of a hog; sah — he; cha — and; dharma-hinah — devoid of dharma.

21One who eats this food casts off every sin and gains dharma, wealth, the fulfilment of desire, immortality and greatness. But the fool who will not eat it loses his dharma and goes the way of a hog.

Verse 22

चैतन्यदेव इह यद्विवशो विभूय
भुङ्क्ते शिवोऽपि यदि तन्नहि खादतीह।
दूरादथागतमिति श्वपचेन वापि
स्पृष्टं विलोक्य बत शूकरतामुपैति॥२२॥

caitanyadeva iha yadvivaśo vibhūya
bhuṅkte śivo'pi yadi tannahi khādatīha|
dūrādathāgatamiti śvapacena vāpi
spṛṣṭaṁ vilokya bata śūkaratāmupaiti||22||

chaitanya-devah — Chaitanyadeva; iha — here; yat — which; vivashah — beside Himself (with love); vibhuya — having appeared; bhunkte — eats; shivah — Shiva; api — even; yadi — if; tat — that; na hi — not; khadati — one eats; iha — here; durat — from afar; atha — or; agatam — come; iti — (thinking) thus; shvapachena — by a dog-eater; va — or; api — even; sprishtam — touched; vilokya — seeing; bata — alas; shukaratam — the state of a hog; upaiti — attains.

22That which Chaitanyadeva, having appeared here, eats beside Himself with love, that which even Shiva eats4 — if anyone here will not eat it, thinking, 'This has been brought from afar,' or seeing that a dog-eater has touched it, alas, he becomes a hog."

Thus ends the eleventh sarga, "The Glory of Sri Mahaprasada" (Shri-mahaprasada-mahima), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The first line of this verse is metrically short in all the editions; the text seems damaged, though the sense is clear.
  2. That is, away from the Deity of Jagannatha, out of the temple.
  3. Narahari ("Hari in human form"): here a name of Krishna.
  4. The opening of the verse is corrupt in all the editions; the rendering is conjectural.
